draft.title: Taxable income
card: all the money a person earns in a year before anything is taken out. It includes wages, salary, commission and interest.
an allowable expense that can be taken off gross income, such as work tools, a work uniform or a union fee. Everyday costs like groceries are not deductions.
gross income − allowable deductions. Income tax is worked out on this amount, not on gross income.
Example: Sam earns $64 000 in a year and has $1 200 of allowable deductions. Taxable income = $64 000 − $1 200 = $62 800.
draft.remember: Taxable income is what is left after deductions, and tax is worked out on it.

a.q: Priya has a gross income of $52 000 and allowable deductions of $900. What is her taxable income?
a.why: Taxable income = gross income − deductions = $52 000 − $900 = $51 100. Adding the deductions gives $52 900, but deductions are taken off, not added.
a.clue: Deductions are taken away from gross income.

b.q: Tom earns $78 500 in a year. He spends $650 on work boots and $350 on a union fee, both allowable. Tax is worked out on which amount?
b.why: Total deductions are $650 + $350 = $1 000. Taxable income = $78 500 − $1 000 = $77 500, and tax is worked out on this. Using $78 500 is tempting, but that is gross income, before deductions.
b.clue: Add the deductions first, then subtract them.

check.summary: No problems found. The arithmetic is correct in both questions, and the definitions of gross income, deductions and taxable income match Australian usage and stay within this point.
